In this lesson we are going to discuss Triacs, Diacs, and Four-Layer Diodes. These components may seem complex, but you will see they are simple combinations of different circuit components.
INTRODUCTIONM

You may be asking yourself, where are these components used and what do they do? Triacs, like SCRs, are mainly used for power control in circuits instead of simple resistance devices. Triacs and SCRs produce much less heat than simple resistive devices..

Diacs and Four-Layer Diodes are used as trigger devices to SCRs and Triacs. Not only do they provide better trigger control, they also provide protection for the trigger circuit. In the first section of this lesson we will explore the use of these components and their use in circuits.

In the second section of this lesson we will experimentally observe a basic Triac circuit while varying different circuit conditions. By observing the Triac operation you will be able to understand the operation of all three devices..

Let's see what we know about the SCR. It doesn't let current flow from cathode to anode unless the gate has been triggered. Once the gate has been triggered, the SCR will continue to allow current flow from cathode to anode until the voltage across the cathode and anode drops below a certain value..
These circuits are called Half-Wave SCR Phase Shifters. In the example below, half of the input current has been removed. This shows that power has been reduced to 50%.

Triac's can be used to reduce a larger power range. Since the Triac is made of two SCRs with anodes connected to cathodes, it operates during both alternations of the sine wave. This allows power to be from 100% to 0% of the input power.

You can see from these two examples how power can be reduced through a Half-Wave SCR Phase Shifter. The important factor to realize is the limitation of the power reduction. A single SCR can reduce the input power to 50%. The input power can be adjusted from half of the input power to 0.
Remember, one of the limiting characteristics of the Half-Wave SCR Phase Shifter is it's range of power reduction. It can reduce input power from 50% to 0% of the input power.

Triacs are also used in other circuit configurations. Triacs are used as switches, especially as high current ON-OFF switches.

If a standard mechanical switch was used high current would jump between the contacts of the switch damaging them. By using a Triac, a small reasonable voltage level can be applied with a mechanical switch to the gate to open the high level current path........

As you can see, there are many beneficial uses for the Triac. Now let's look at the use of a Diac and Four-Layer Diode. A Four-Layer Diode is an SCR with the gate attached internally. When the input voltage has reached a certain level, the Four-Layer Diode will begin to conduct.

The Four-layer diode will then continue to conduct until the input voltage falls below a certain level. Just like the similarity between the SCR and the Triac, the Diac is two Four-layer diodes connected in reverse..

A Four-Layer Diode is normally used with SCRs since conduction is only required during one alternation, the Diac is used with Triacs. The main purpose of these devices is to limit the input current to the gate until a certain level has been reached..

Since power reducing circuits are normally connected directly to a power source, Diacs and Four-Layer Diodes provide protection to the circuit. As you can see, Triacs, Diacs and Four-Layer Diodes are made of SCRs..
